gap: R1-1 — ISO 9241-110's seven interaction (dialogue) principle NAMES were paywalled at #236 and were deliberately NOT entered from memory.

source.author: Rolf Molich / DialogDesign, Stenløse, Denmark
source.authority_class: PRACTITIONER SUMMARY, NOT THE STANDARD. This is Molich's page. It is a licensed secondary, not ISO text.
source.authority_receipt: "The principles and the explanations of the principles are taken from the ISO standard"
source.reproduction_licence_receipt: "Text from the draft international standard ISO/FDIS 9241-110.2020 is reproduced with permission"
source.licence_note: The page states its permission comes from Danish Standards Foundation (DS), and that the reproduced text is from the DRAFT (ISO/FDIS 9241-110.2020), not the published standard. Anything client-facing should cite the published standard, not this page.

edition_and_year_as_the_page_states_it.count_receipt: "The ISO standard 9241-110 from 2020 defines seven dialogue principles"
edition_and_year_as_the_page_states_it.edition_stated: ed-2 — inferred from the page's own purchase link, https://www.iso.org/obp/ui/#iso:std:iso:9241:-110:ed-2:v1:en
edition_and_year_as_the_page_states_it.url_slug_mismatch: The page URL slug reads 'isos-dialogue-principles-2019' while the heading, title and body all say 2020. Cite 2020; the 2019 in the slug is a stale slug, not a date claim.
edition_and_year_as_the_page_states_it.our_words: The page attributes seven dialogue principles to ISO 9241-110:2020, second edition.

scale_of_the_standard_beyond_the_names.our_words: The seven names are the top of a much larger structure; a graph node built from names alone carries about a fifteenth of the standard.
scale_of_the_standard_beyond_the_names.receipt: "20 categories of recommendations, 65 recommendations, and about 140 examples take up 15 densely printed pages"
scale_of_the_standard_beyond_the_names.consequence: Grade the node on what we actually hold: seven names plus one definition sentence each. The recommendations underneath remain unfetched and unpriced.

principles.our_words: The system fits the shape of the work, not the shape of the technology used to build it.
principles.receipt: "supports the users in the completion of their tasks"
principles.molich_personal_comment_our_words: Molich reads this as 'meeting user needs' and notes it is covered by neither the 1990 Molich-Nielsen heuristics nor Nielsen's 1994 set — so it is the principle the famous heuristic lists omit.

principles.our_words: What the thing can do, and how to use it, is legible from the interface without the user having to poke at it to find out.
principles.receipt: "make its capabilities and use immediately obvious to the user"

principles.our_words: Behaviour is predictable from context and from the conventions people already carry into it.
principles.receipt: "behavior is predictable based on the context of use and commonly accepted conventions"

principles.our_words: The system can be explored safely, teaches itself where it must, and minimises what has to be learned at all.
principles.receipt: "supports discovery of its capabilities and how to use them, allows exploration"

principles.our_words: The user sets the pace, the order and the personalisation; the system does not take the wheel.
principles.receipt: "allows the user to maintain control of the user interface and the interactions"

principles.our_words: Errors are prevented where possible, tolerated where not, and recoverable when they land.
principles.receipt: "assists the user in avoiding errors and in case of identifiable errors treats them tolerantly"
principles.sub_structure_our_words: Named sub-parts: use error avoidance, use error tolerance, use error recovery.
principles.molich_personal_comment_our_words: Molich says these are three separate principles that the ISO committee merged for political reasons — worth carrying, because a graph that treats this as one node loses the avoid/tolerate/recover distinction that actually drives design decisions.

principles.our_words: Functions and information are presented so that continuing to use the system is inviting rather than grudging.
principles.receipt: "presents functions and information in an inviting and motivating manner supporting continued interaction"
principles.molich_personal_comment_our_words: Molich adds that engagement must be ethical and is inappropriate for some system classes, naming sports betting. That caveat puts this principle one inch from the DSA Article 25 line already in the register as pr-dsa25.

what_this_does_and_does_not_prove.proves: The seven names, their order, and one definition sentence each, read off a page that states its own permission to reproduce them.
what_this_does_and_does_not_prove.does_not_prove: The published ISO 9241-110:2020 wording (the page reproduces the FDIS draft), the 20 recommendation categories, the 65 recommendations, or the ~140 examples.
what_this_does_and_does_not_prove.residual_price: Purchase of the standard, or a fetch of a licensed full text, to move from names to recommendations.
